headline: Grizzlies roll past short-handed Warriors 126-98 for a fifth straight win
text: MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- — Jaylen Wells had 22 points and Cedric Coward scored 19 to lead the Memphis Grizzlies to their fifth straight win on Thursday night, 126-98 over the short-handed Golden State Warriors . Cam Boozer and Olivier Maxence-Prosper scored 16 apiece for the Grizzlies, who never trailed and led by 34 points in the fourth quarter. Javon Small added 14 points. Charles Bassey finished with 16 points and 13 boards for the Warriors, who got 15 points each from Brandin Podziemski and Will Richard . The Warriors, who went 0-5 on their road trip, shot 5 of 29 from long range without the injured Stephen Curry . Curry missed his fourth consecutive game. He tore an oblique muscle during a loss at Houston that began the five-game road trip. Draymond Green sat out with a right elbow injury. The injury plagued Warriors used their 12th different starting lineup this season. The Grizzlies were without starters Ty Jerome , the team’s leading scorer, and center Zach Edey . Memphis also lost Jerami Grant early in the second quarter after he landed awkwardly on his left leg after making a 3-pointer. Golden State trimmed the Memphis lead to six points in the opening minute of the third quarter, but the Grizzlies responded by gradually extending their lead to 20 in the closing two minutes of the third quarter. Memphis shot 51% in the first half and built an 18-point lead midway through the second quarter. Although Golden State struggled in the first half — going 14 of 36 for 37%, including 3 of 16 from long range — it only trailed 55-47 at halftime. Up next Warriors: Host Boston at home on Sunday. Grizzlies: At Minnesota Saturday where they’ll attempt to open the season with a ninth straight victory on the road. ---- See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Lillard scores 33 in return to Milwaukee as Blazers win 124-114. Bucks have lost 12 straight
text: MILWAUKEE -- — Damian Lillard scored a season-high 33 points in his return to Milwaukee and the Trail Blazers won 124-114 to hand the Bucks their 12th consecutive loss on Thursday night. The only longer skid in Bucks' history came in March 1996, when they lost 15 straight games, according to Sportradar. That team went on to finish 25-57. Milwaukee’s 1-15 record is its worst mark ever through the first 16 games of a season. This game marked the first time Lillard had played at Milwaukee since getting waived in the summer of 2025 after two seasons with the Bucks. Lillard had accompanied the Blazers to Milwaukee for a 115-103 victory last season, though his Achilles injury prevented him from playing that night. The Bucks were playing one night after losing 137-130 at Miami in their first matchup with Giannis Antetokounmpo since trading the two-time MVP to the Heat last summer. Scoot Henderson had a season-high 27 points and Jrue Holiday added 22 as the Blazers snapped a two-game skid by winning a game that included 20 lead changes and eight ties. Toumani Camara scored all 18 of his points in the second half. Tyler Herro scored 19 points for Milwaukee. Bucks rookie Nate Ament made his second start and had 18 points and nine rebounds — both career highs. Kasparas Jakučionis also had 18 points. The Bucks were playing without Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner due to shoulder bruises. Portland’s Deni Avdija sat out a second straight game with a sore left foot and Ja Morant missed an 11th consecutive game due to a hamstring strain. After Herro's driving basket cut Portland's lead to 115-114 with 3:18 remaining, Portland scored the game's final nine points. Up next Trail Blazers: At New York on Saturday night. Bucks: At Philadelphia on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Knicks fend off the Timberwolves 102-99 behind 22 points from Karl-Anthony Towns vs. his former team
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Karl-Anthony Towns scored 17 of his 22 points in the first half and grabbed 12 rebounds against his former team to help the New York Knicks hang on and beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 102-99 on Thursday night. Jalen Brunson had 21 points and seven assists and OG Anunoby added 15 points for the Knicks (9-6), who won their third straight game despite nearly squandering a 19-point, third-quarter lead and failing to score over the final 3:26. Ayo Dosunmu cut the deficit to three with a 3-pointer with 2:34 remaining and would've tied it on the next possession with another swish from deep, but that didn't count because of a premature whistle for a shot clock violation. Replay review determined LaMelo Ball 's jumper had grazed the rim. Ball missed a tying 3-point attempt with 9.9 seconds left, and the Timberwolves couldn't get another shot off. Jonathan Kuminga had 23 points for the Timberwolves (11-5) in his return from a two-game absence because of a bruised right shoulder. Ball had 15 points on 6-for-21 shooting. Towns, who was traded to the Knicks in 2024 after nine years with the Timberwolves, is having another standout season as he seeks a contract extension . He was greeted loudly and warmly by the crowd before the game and brought his best again to Minnesota. After losing his balance on a contested layup, Towns fell flat on his back next to his father, Karl Towns, who helped him up from his baseline seat. Towns had 32 points and 20 rebounds for the Knicks in a 133-107 victory two years ago in his first game in Minnesota after the trade. Last season, he had 40 points and 13 rebounds in his return during a 115-104 defeat , his first to the Timberwolves. Up next Knicks: vs. Portland on Saturday. Timberwolves: vs. Memphis on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Wembanyama and Castle help Spurs bounce back from loss to Pistons and beat Clippers 124-112
text: SAN ANTONIO -- — Victor Wembanyama had 32 points and 11 rebounds, Stephon Castle added 21 points and 12 assists, and the San Antonio Spurs held off the Los Angeles Clippers for a 124-112 victory on Thursday night. Julian Champagnie added 20 points for San Antonio, which bounced back from a 105-93 loss to Detroit on Tuesday that snapped its 12-game winning streak. Wembanyama was 13 for 26 in scoring at least 30 points for the seventh time this season. Darius Garland and Brook Lopez had 23 points apiece for Los Angeles. San Antonio lost Dylan Harper to injury in the loss to the Pistons and he is expected to miss one to three weeks with a strained left hip he sustained with a minute remaining after slipping as he attempted to plant his feet. With Harper out, Jordan McLaughlin filled in the rotation and had five rebounds, three assists and no turnovers. The Spurs outscored the Clippers by 16 points in his 11 minutes. Castle's steal and pass to Champagnie for a 3-pointer gave San Antonio a 105-97 lead with 8 minutes remaining, but Lopez and Max Strus hit back-to-back 3-pointers to cut the deficit. It was a pattern the Spurs struggled with all game. San Antonio was allowing a league-low 32.9 3-point attempts per game but Los Angeles finished 17 for 42. The Spurs were 11 for 31 on 3-pointers. After a sluggish start, Castle's 3-pointer gave the Spurs their first double-digit lead at 38-28 four minutes into the second quarter. San Antonio is 12-1 when leading by double digits this season. Strus finished with 18 points and was 5 for 8 on 3-pointers. Up next Clippers: At Dallas on Saturday. Spurs: Host New Orleans on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
